summary: IAM deny on sts:TagSession prevents analytics-ingest-role exchange, blocking dedicated training cluster provisioning
description:
Issue summary: Automated dedicated training cluster provisioning failing during service-account exchange. Impact: New dedicated clusters for analytics batch jobs cannot be provisioned in prod-us-east; delays affecting scheduled training jobs and on-call escalations. Environment: prod-us-east, provisioning executed from infra-pipeline CI (service principal: infra-ci-sa) performing AssumeRole -> sts:TagSession to set tags required by org SCPs. Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger infra-pipeline job that calls AssumeRole on arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/dedicated-provisioner.
2) dedicated-provisioner attempts to assume analytics-ingest-role with session tags (owner, env, team).
3) STS call fails with AccessDenied for sts:TagSession.
Observed logs / errors:
- sts:AssumeRole returning AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:TagSession for resource arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/analytics-ingest-role
- CloudTrail snippet (2026-03-10T03:12:44Z): eventName=AssumeRole, errorMessage=User: arn:aws:sts::... is not authorized to perform: sts:TagSession
Attempts made so far:
- Verified pipeline IAM policy (infra-pipeline role) includes sts:AssumeRole but not explicitly sts:TagSession.
- Confirmed analytics-ingest-role has a trust policy allowing AssumeRole from dedicated-provisioner but also an org SCP requiring session tags for access to particular resources.
- Temporarily tested with a user session that has sts:TagSession allowed and provisioning succeeds (proof-of-concept).
Impact assessment:
- Affects all provisioning flows that rely on session tags to satisfy org SCP tag conditions. Estimated 3-5 urgent cluster requests blocked per day.
Desired outcome: Restore provisioning workflow while maintaining org-level guardrails around required tags.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: infra-pipeline role has not been granted sts:TagSession (or a permission boundary/SCP blocks it). Cross-check against org-level SCPs shows a deny-if-no-session-tag rule (Condition: aws:RequestTag). Possible causes: (A) recent org SCP rollout tightened tag enforcement (rolled 2026-03-09) and infra roles not updated; (B) permission boundary on dedicated-provisioner overrides sts permissions; (C) session was attempted via chained assume-role path that strips TagSession rights. Evidence: CloudTrail shows error immediately at AssumeRole step and dedicated-provisioner logs show no successful TagSession token. Reproduced in staging by removing TagSession from test-role and observing same failure. Next steps: 1) Request scoped policy change to grant sts:TagSession to infra-pipeline role for the specific ARNs or call-from principal; 2) If SCP is blocking, request exception for provisioning window or modify SCP to allow calls when assuming via dedicated-provisioner; 3) Add circuit-breaker in pipeline to surface clearer error and fall back to manual provisioning runbooks.
Temporary mitigation tested: Re-running job under a user with broader sts permissions succeeded; not acceptable as permanent fix.

2026-03-12 14:12 - Security (Elena Morales): Org SCP denies calls without required tags. We can add a scoped allow for the infra-pipeline role for a time-bound window, or alter the SCP to allow TagSession only when call originates from our management account. Need justification and risk acceptance from Infra.
2026-03-13 09:02 - Leo Patel: Created draft minimal policy for infra-pipeline to include sts:TagSession with conditions on aws:RequestTag and aws:TagKeys. Preparing PR and will link.
resolution: In progress: Infra PR prepared to add sts:TagSession for infra-pipeline role with strict conditions (aws:RequestTag scope, allowed TagKeys list, and aws:CalledVia management-account ARN). Security approved a temporary, timebound exception for 48 hours to unblock urgent provisioning while we deploy the scoped policy. Long term: update CI role provisioning templates to include sts:TagSession where session tags are required and add automated policy checks in repo CI. Follow-up ticket created to audit all CI roles against org SCPs and to add observability to surface this error earlier.
